prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: unique decorative background for Willis Wee's Work / career history page, part of an established midnight pixel-art personal website.
Primary request: create a quiet coastal maker's workshop and a winding path representing a lifetime of building. Output a very tall portrait image, 768 by 2048 pixels.
Input image: the provided seaside desk image is STYLE AND PALETTE REFERENCE ONLY. Do not reproduce its person, desk setup, or wide composition.
Scene: a modest open-sided timber workshop on a rocky tropical cove at blue hour, a warm amber lantern above the doorway, a simple wooden workbench visible inside. A worn wooden boardwalk winds from the bottom foreground toward the workshop, with a calm deep-blue sea and distant headland behind it. A few coastal leaves frame one edge. No people.
Composition: this artwork lives entirely in a narrow LEFT sidebar alongside a reading panel; do not put the subject on the right of a wide canvas. Tall portrait 768x2048. Keep the top 35 percent quiet, dark navy sky and distant water, because a navigation box will sit there. Put the recognizable workshop and its warm entrance between 50 and 74 percent down the image; keep all essential features within the central 65 percent of the canvas width so a narrow crop still works. The boardwalk leads down through the lower quarter. Favor a clear silhouette and a small, memorable scene over crowded detail.
Style/medium: handcrafted high-quality pixel-art adventure-game scenery matching the reference's crisp blocky contours, restrained dithering, layered deep blues and warm wooden materials. Not vector, not low-poly, not photographic. Simpler than the reference, made for the edge of a long reading page.
Lighting: low-contrast midnight navy, muted teal sea, subdued copper sky near horizon, a small inviting pool of warm amber lantern light. No bright sunset occupying the page, no neon.
Constraints: no lettering, no logos, no UI, no signs, no frame, no watermark. No tent, no open book or compass from the separate Guide page. No characters or sloth mascots. Keep the art unique to a coastal workshop.
processing: WebP quality 88, effort 6; no creative edits or resizing
